Formester Vs Fillout

Formester

Formester is a hosted form builder with a built-in AI generator, offline forms that install as an app on phones and tablets, and 50 GB of file storage on the Business plan. Free includes unlimited responses, the AI form creator, offline PWA install, and native payments. Personal at $12 a month removes branding and adds conditional logic. Business at $45 a month covers unlimited responses, API access, PDF exports, an MCP server, and 25 team seats.

Fillout

Fillout is a hosted form builder best known for native two-way sync with Airtable, Notion, and Google Sheets, and a generous free plan with 1,000 responses a month and unlimited forms. Pricing climbs to $15 Starter, $40 Pro, and $75 Business. Strong fit for teams whose work already lives inside Airtable or Notion. No native offline mode and no dedicated mobile app.

The honest read

Why teams leave Fillout.

Four reasons teams switching to Formester have given us. Sourced from G2, Capterra, Reddit reviews and vendor pricing pages, not made up.

No offline mode for mobile collection.

Fillout does not ship a native offline mobile app. Field teams collecting data without connectivity (events, surveys, in-store) hit a wall the moment the network drops.

EU data residency only on higher tiers.

EU customers who need GDPR-grade data residency are pushed to the Team or Enterprise plans. Smaller EU teams describe building workflows on Starter, then discovering they need to upgrade for residency.

Fewer payment gateways than incumbents.

Fillout's payment integration list is narrower than Jotform's 40+ gateways. Teams running international payment flows (Mollie, regional providers) hit gaps.

Pricing climbs fast above the free tier.

Free is generous (1,000 responses per month), but Starter is $15/mo, Pro $40/mo, Business $75/mo yearly. The $480 to $900 jump from annual Pro ($480/yr) to annual Business ($900/yr) surprises teams who expected a smoother ramp.

Why teams switch

Why teams choose Formester over Fillout.

Eight reasons buyers searching for a Fillout alternative tell us they made the switch. Each item ties to a specific Formester plan or feature, not a marketing line.

AI form generator on the free plan

Prompt, PDF, or question list. Formester drafts the form in seconds, on the free plan.

Native payments included on the free plan

Stripe and PayPal integration on day one. No add-on, no upgrade. Most teams switching from Fillout cite this as the deciding feature.

Conditional logic on Personal at $12/mo annual

Field-level rules across inputs, not just section branching. Show, hide, skip, route, calculate. Personal at $12/mo annual.

REST API + MCP server for AI agents

Hosted REST API on Business plus an MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, or any compatible model.

Field teams collect without signal. Submissions sync when the network returns. Free plan, no app store install.

Custom domain on Business, branded URL on Personal

Forms live on your domain, not a vendor URL. Personal unlocks a custom subdomain; Business unlocks the full custom domain.

Multi-language with AI translation

180+ languages via AI translation on Business. One source form, respondent picks their language, edits stay in sync.

Privacy-first: no AI training on your data

GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA compliant. Customer Data is not used to train AI models. Honest about SOC 2 and ISO 27001, we do not certify them yet.

Migration

How to switch from Fillout to Formester in 3 steps.

From "I want to leave Fillout" to "the new form is live" without losing data or missing submissions.

1

Export your existing entries.

In Fillout, open Forms → Submissions → Export CSV. Capture each form's responses as a CSV. Pull integration logs (Airtable / Notion sync history) for reference.

Time: 5 to 10 minutes for a typical 5-form workspace.

2

Rebuild with the AI form generator.

Sign up for Formester (free, no card). Open the AI form generator, paste a description of the Fillout form, or upload the questions list. The generator drafts the structure with field types, validation, and conditional logic. Edit the labels and apply your branding.

Time: 10 to 20 minutes per form for a typical 10-field form.

3

Re-point your integrations.

Update the destination on your Airtable / Notion / Slack / Zapier flows from Fillout's webhook endpoints to Formester's. Test one submission, confirm the integration fires, then archive the Fillout form.

Time: 10 to 15 minutes; keep Fillout active for a week as a fallback.

Honest comparison

When Fillout is still the better choice.

Two real cases where Fillout beats Formester. We are the alternative for the rest, and that is okay.

Your forms live downstream in Airtable or Notion.

  • If your team's source of truth is an Airtable base or a Notion workspace, Fillout's native bindings will be cleaner than anything Formester ships through Zapier.
  • Their UI is purpose-built around the database connection; Formester's is purpose-built around the form output.
  • Honest tradeoff: that Airtable / Notion polish is the reason to stay on Fillout despite the lower free-plan ceiling on Formester.

You need SOC 2 or ISO 27001 on your security questionnaire.

  • Fillout is SOC 2 compliant; Formester is not yet.
  • If your buying review requires formal SOC 2 or ISO 27001 attestations, Fillout clears that gate today and Formester does not.
  • Honest tradeoff: formal attestations are a real win for regulated buyers. We're a fit when offline collection, AI on free, or REST API + MCP matter more.

Privacy and data ownership

Your form data is yours. We don't train on it.

The prompts you write, the AI-generated form structures, and the responses respondents submit are all Customer Data. Per Section 4.4 of our Data Processing Addendum, Formester does not use Customer Data to train AI models, run advertising, run analytics, or feed marketing. The Google Gemini integration that drafts forms inherits the same boundary.

Your account is encrypted at rest, responses move over TLS, and payment data carries an additional AES-256 layer through Stripe. We are GDPR, UK GDPR, and CCPA compliant. We are not SOC 2, ISO 27001, or HIPAA certified yet, and we say so on the security page rather than implying otherwise. If your buying review requires those today, we'll tell you up front.
